proofUses.reason: A backward-flow invariant rectangle and Koebe distortion control a full height-time strip by one derivative at its deterministic left endpoint.

A deterministic mesh of length 4^(-n)/(n+1)^2 makes Brownian oscillations summable; the derivative tail has a strict lambda-2-sigma*q margin. Vertical telescoping is uniform in time, and countable horizons/exponents give one probability-one event.
Adjacent mesh intervals and uniform radial error give u^(sigma/2)(1+abs(log u))^sigma; every beta<sigma0/2 is admissible. These are sufficient, not optimal, exponents.
Fixed-time Holder extension and the measurable radial Cauchy criterion permit Fubini on integer time horizons. This gives no uniform convergence or full kappa-eight trace construction.
